## Overview

**MATISSE** stands for MATLAB Toolbox for vital rates surveillance. It brings together methods for studying cancer rates. Read the scientific background in [*Advances in statistical methods for cancer surveillance research: an age-period-cohort perspective*](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/oncology/articles/10.3389/fonc.2023.1332429/full).

MATISSE includes the analyses available in the [Age-Period-Cohort Analysis Web Tool](https://dceg.cancer.gov/tools/analysis/apc). It also provides comparative APC analysis, methods for smoothing Lexis diagrams, and semiparametric APC analysis (SAGE). A **Lexis diagram** displays rates by age and calendar period. Use [Related methods and publications](resources.html#related-methods-and-publications) to learn more about each method.

MATISSE is free to use. Open it in [MATLAB Online](https://www.mathworks.com/products/matlab-online.html), or use a local copy of MATLAB if you have a license. Check the current MATLAB Online access terms when you sign in.

## Design

MATISSE uses an [object-oriented design](https://www.mathworks.com/company/technical-articles/introduction-to-object-oriented-programming-in-matlab.html). An **object** stores data or a fitted model. A **class** defines a type of object. A **method** is a function that works with that type of object. Start with these four classes:

-   A `rates` object stores rates by age and calendar period.
-   An `apc` object stores an APC analysis fitted to a `rates` object.
-   A `tbl` object stores a table of values with row and column labels.
-   A `matrix` object stores values and their uncertainty. It carries that uncertainty through calculations, so you do not need to write separate code for each step.

The core classes shipped in the toolbox:

| Class            | Purpose                                                                                     |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `rates`          | Age-specific event rates over time (Lexis diagrams); descriptive plots and age-standardized rates (ASRs)        |
| `apc`            | The new age-period-cohort model                                                             |
| `epiphany`       | Exploratory comparative age-period-cohort analysis                                          |
| `capricorn`      | Hypothesis-based comparative age-period-cohort analysis                                     |
| `joinpoint`      | Joinpoint regression                                                                        |
| `sift`           | Singular-value adaptive kernel filtration                                                   |
| `sage`           | Semiparametric age-period-cohort analysis                                                   |
| `panko`          | Kernel smoothing utilities feeding into `sift`                                              |
| `tbl` / `matrix` | Lightweight labeled-data and error-propagating array containers underlying everything above |

### System map

**Video:** [Watch the system map guide on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6frwitiOJ_Y) (22 sec).

Use the system map to find the classes and methods you need. Each class is a line, and its methods are the stops. The `rates` and `matrix` classes are hubs that connect parts of the toolbox. Add the toolbox to your MATLAB path, then run this command to open the map:

``` matlab
matisse('map')
```

![MATISSE system map](images/system_map.png){fig-alt="Map of MATISSE classes and methods, styled after a subway map" width="90%"}

## Scripting with MATISSE

A working example gives you a starting point for your own analysis. Open a live script (`.mlx`) from the user's guide in Downloads. Copy the relevant section into a new script, then change the data inputs. Try small changes in the MATLAB Command Window before adding them to your script.

## Getting help

The built-in help explains how each function works and which inputs it needs. Use it when you are unsure how to run a command. Enter these commands in the MATLAB Command Window:

``` matlab
help rates/rates          % help for a specific class
methods rates              % list every method of a class
help rates/fill             % help for a specific method
doc('rates')                 % open help in a standalone window
```
